newsitem.title: UK: Dlr edges higher in late Europe amid weaker mark.
newsitem.headline: Dlr edges higher in late Europe amid weaker mark.

text.p: The dollar edged higher in late European trade, clearing 1.52 marks as stops were triggered amid overall mark weakness.

"Stops went above 1.5150 marks and then again above 1.52 marks," said a Swiss bank dealer. "The mark/yen dip below 74 helped and it's mainly mark weakness and the tail-end of the lira ERM re-entry effect that's driving things now."

The market showed little reaction to a slight dip in U.S. October housing starts, which dropped 1.5 percent to a 3.97 million annual rate. An average of analysts forecasts pointed to a rate of four million.
The dollar was at 1.5201/06 per mark at 1632 GMT, off a session high of 1.5230. It stood at 1.5045/55 late Friday in Europe.

A stronger dollar against the Swiss franc was also helping dollar/mark, clearing resistance at 1.28 francs to touch a high for the day of 1.2865. It was still firm by late trade but had retreated to 1.2840/50 against 1.2690/00 late Friday.

"Much of the dollar strength is still part of the lira-ERM effect which has hit the mark," said Roger Francis, senior analyst at IBJ International. "The decent German CPI data has also been some help."
West German preliminary inflation indicated a 0.1 percent drop for November and 1.4 percent rise year-on-year compared with 1.5 percent in October.

Analysts said this data indicated German inflation is hardly a problem and that higher German interest rates are still some way away. Many see stable rates in the foreseeable future with some seeing the possibility of a rate cut in the early part of next year.
The lira's ERM re-entry at the weekend was not a surprise but dealers said the central rate of 990 per mark was against general expectations of a 1,000 lire mid-point.

The lira traded around its new ERM mid-rate, testing below the 990 level in afternoon trade as its entry into the grid rekindled optimism about Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU), hurting the German mark.
The French franc was also firmer against the mark as the lira's firm ERM rate was seen easing the recent pressure of Frances' so-called franc fort currency policy.

By 1655 GMT, mark/lira was trading at 990.00/50 against 997.90/8.25 late Friday. Mark/French franc stood at 3.3852/56, off a session low of 3.3815 franc but still below late Friday's rate of 3.3908/12.
Sterling was softer in late European trade, off its 32-month highs against the mark and extending its day's losses against the dollar.

Dealers said there was some nervousness ahead of the UK 1997/98 budget Tuesday. Overall expectations are for a cautious budget which is seen underpinning sterling as well as ongoing speculation of further UK rate rises.
Sterling/mark was trading at 2.5385/96 at 1706 GMT, down from its 32-month peak of 2.5476 but still above 2.5288/99 on Friday. Cable stood at $1.6685/95 from $1.6808/18 Friday.
